extended:
**Bring’s curve: old and new**

*RESEARCH ARTICLE*

46 pp, 25 sections.

**Abstract.** Bring’s curve, the unique Riemann surface of genus 4 with automorphism group S5, has many exceptional properties. We review, give new proofs of, and extend a number of these including giving the complete realisation of the automorphism group for a plane curve model, identifying a new elliptic quotient of the curve and the modular curve X0(50), providing a complete description of the orbit decomposition of the theta characteristics, and identifying the unique invariant characteristic with the divisor of the Szeg˝o kernel. In achieving this we have used modern computational tools in Sagemath, Macaulay2, and Maple, for which notebooks demonstrating calculations are provided.

**Outline.** Front matter; Bring's curve: old and new; Abstract; 1 Introduction; 2 Defining equations and elementary properties; 2.1 Basic properties; 2.2 The period matrix; 2.3 The automorphism group; 3 Geometric points; 3.1 Weierstrass points; 3.2 Vertices and face-centres; 4 Quotients by subgroups; 4.1 Genera of quotients; 4.2 Relations between quotients; 4.3 Quotients by a 4- and 2,2-cycle; 4.4 Quotients by a 3-cycle; 4.5 Quotients by a transposition; 4.6 Summarising
